subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — throughput guarantees & reserved commit terms
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@axiomhealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Axiom Health Procurement <procurement@axiomhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity — initial ask on throughput guarantees and pricing

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week — we liked the latency profile on the 13B model. Before we move into procurement, procurement needs clear throughput guarantees (tokens/sec and req/sec), p50/p95 latency targets, and a brief measurement methodology we can include in the SOW.

High-level ask:
- Our peak workload is ~600 concurrent infer requests (avg 40 tokens/request) and some spikes to 1.2k concurrent.
- We need 95% of requests to be <120 ms on our interactive endpoints for 8k token context jobs (these are chat-like completions).
- We also care about steady-state tokens/sec for batch scoring (single-threaded, long sequences).

Can you propose a committed GPU pool sizing, committed monthly throughput guarantees, and the discount schedule for reserved commits? Also let us know how you’ll measure/validate those numbers during acceptance.

Liam
Senior Platform Engineer
Axiom Health

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity — initial ask on throughput guarantees and pricing

Team — forwarding Axiom's ask. Key constraints: interactive p95 < 120ms for ~8k context, spikes to 1.2k concurrent. They want committed sizing + discount tiers and an acceptance measurement plan we can sign into the SOW.

Drafting notes / questions:
- Do we recommend 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (or 12x for headroom)? We should show both a baseline commit and a burstable tier.
- Pricing: our standard reserved discount bands (10/20/30%) based on 3/6/12 month commits — any room to tighten for strategic reference customer?
- Measurement: we should require a shared test harness (we run the test from their VPC in dedicated environment), 30-minute sustained windows, warmup of 5 minutes, KV-cache cold vs warm reporting. Include clear pass/fail: sustained throughput >= committed tokens/sec for 95% of measurement windows and p95 latency <= target for interactive endpoints.

Posting an internal draft below; please reply with edits.

—V

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity — initial ask on throughput guarantees and pricing

Vivek / all — suggested edits below to make the offer customer-friendly but protective for us. Short version: two-tier commit with a short acceptance/validation window and explicit measurement steps.

Offer summary (proposed wording):
- Committed pool: 10 x A100-equivalent GPUs (baseline) — supports ~700 concurrent interactive sessions at 8k context with p95 <= 120ms for our 13B optimised infer path.
- Burstable capacity: additional 4 GPUs available for short-term spikes (soft limit, best-effort).
- Committed throughput guarantee: 100M tokens/day (equivalent to ~2.5M tokens/hour sustained) with measurement at token/sec granularity.
- Interactive SLOs: p50 <= 25ms, p95 <= 120ms for chat endpoints at target concurrency; request/sec measured over 1-minute windows.

Validation & measurement methodology (detailed in attached test plan):
- Test harness: joint repo; Redwood runs in Axiom test VPC endpoint with identical routing/policy to production.
- Warmup: 10-minute warmup followed by a 30-minute measurement window for each test vector.
- Conditions: KV cache cold and warm runs recorded separately; autoscaling disabled for the baseline test.
- Metrics: per-second tokens/sec, requests/sec, latency histograms (p50/p90/p95), GPU utilization, and tail latency traces. Logs and traces shared via Drive link.
- Pass criteria: during measurement windows, committed tokens/sec must be >= 95% of target and interactive p95 <= 120ms. If the baseline fails, we provide remediation plan and 1 additional validation run.

Pricing & discounts:
- 6-month commit: 20% off list for committed pool (billing monthly).
- 12-month commit: 30% off list + 5% additional credit for multi-region (if they want EU later).
- Spike overage price: metered at standard on-demand rate; we can offer burst credits as a one-time concession.

I'll attach a short SOW blurb and the throughput validation plan. Suggest V signs off on wording + commercial concession (one-month trial credit) before we send.

—Ben
Director, Sales

[Attachment: 20270407-dedicated-throughput-test-plan.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]

Cc: Axiom Health Procurement <procurement@axiomhealth.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — throughput guarantees & reserved commit terms

Hi Liam — thanks for the details and patience. Attached is our proposed offer and the measurement plan (see Drive link above). Summary below tailored to Axiom's workload:

1) Sizing & capacity
- Baseline committed pool: 10 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved). This is sized to sustain ~700 concurrent interactive sessions on the 13B model at 8k context with the optimised runtime.
- Burstable headroom: +4 GPUs on a best-effort basis for short spikes (we recommend enabling burst credits in month 1).

2) Throughput & SLO guarantees (contract language suggestion)
- Committed throughput: 100,000,000 tokens/day. Measurements reported in tokens/sec and requests/sec (aggregated to 1-min and 1-hour windows).
- Interactive latency targets (for chat endpoints): p50 <= 25ms, p95 <= 120ms measured across 1-minute windows at target concurrency.
- Requests/sec: measured over 1-minute windows; expected baseline handling of ~700 concurrent requests with graceful degradation beyond committed headroom.

3) Measurement methodology (acceptance testing)
- Shared test harness: Redwood will run acceptance tests from Axiom’s test VPC endpoint (we will provide a small agent image you run in your test VPC).
- Warmup: 10 minute warmup per test vector; measurement window: 30 minutes. Each test vector exercised twice (cold cache + warm cache).
- Metrics collected: per-second tokens/sec, requests/sec, latency histograms (p50/p90/p95), GPU util, KV cache hit rate, and full traces for tail cases. Results uploaded to the shared Drive link and a summary report provided.
- Acceptance criteria: during measurement windows, sustained tokens/sec must be >= 95% of committed throughput and interactive p95 must be <= 120ms. If tests fail, Redwood will execute a remediation plan (tunings or additional capacity) followed by one re-test at no additional charge.

4) Commercial terms
- 6 month reserved commit: 20% discount off hosted list pricing for compute; monthly billing.
- 12 month reserved commit: 30% discount + 5% multi-region credit if they add EU later.
- Overage: On-demand metering for spikes; we offer a one-time burst credit in month 1 (equivalent to 500k tokens) as a concession for the pilot.

5) Next steps
- If this looks good we’ll attach the SOW language into your procurement packet and schedule a 2-hour validation window during a mutually agreed date (we suggest 2 business days availability).

Attachments: 20270407-dedicated-throughput-test-plan.pdf; RDW-Axiom-SOW-draft.docx

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the measurement plan.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — throughput guarantees & reserved commit terms

Vivek / Ben — appreciate the clear proposal. A few quick clarifying notes from procurement and platform:
- Can you convert the committed throughput into an equivalent sustained tokens/sec target (e.g., X tokens/sec over 1-hour window)? Procurement wants that explicit.
- For the SLOs, can you add p99 for the interactive endpoint (as an advisory, not breach-based) so we can see tail behavior?
- Please include a clause that the acceptance testing will run under a mutually-agreed traffic mix (we'll provide a representative client trace).

Assuming those edits, procurement is comfortable with the 6- or 12-month option; we prefer 12-month if the EU credit is in the SOW. Can we target a validation window the week of Apr 26?

I'll wait for updated SOW language and the tokens/sec equivalence. Thanks — Liam
